title: Advent at home
hookLine: a wreath, a Jesse tree, quiet evenings
tomorrow: so when does Christmas actually end?

lines: TREE IN THE GARAGE TILL CHRISTMAS EVE.
cards: The neighbors' lights went up the weekend after Thanksgiving. The radio has been playing carols for weeks.
And in some Catholic homes, the tree stays in the garage until Christmas Eve, and the house is quiet, with purple candles, for four weeks.

In other Catholic homes, the tree goes up early and the waiting happens with the lights on. Same Church, same season, two very different living rooms. Both families have their reasons, and both reasons are worth hearing.

teach.b: The Church's own description gives both sides something.
Its norms for the liturgical year say Advent has two faces: getting ready for Christmas, when Christ's first coming is remembered, and turning minds toward his coming at the end of time.
And they call it a season of devout and joyful expectation. View one, the quiet house. Advent is its own season, not early Christmas.
A wreath with four candles, one more lit each week. A Jesse tree, hung with small ornaments for the people who waited through the Old Testament: Adam, Noah, Abraham, David.
Advent hymns, like O come, O come, Emmanuel, with the carols saved for later. Its best case: if you feast for a month first, Christmas Day arrives tired.

teach.h: THE QUIET HOUSE: WAITING MAKES JOY LAND.
teach.b: The waiting is what makes the joy land.

teach.h: THE EARLY TREE: JOY THAT WAITS.
teach.b: View two, the early tree. Joyful expectation is still joy. Lights in the darkest stretch of the year are a sign of what's coming, and a family decorating together on a December night is already waiting together.
Its best case: a home isn't a church, and kids learn a season by living inside it.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the third Sunday of Advent is called Gaudete, Latin for rejoice, from Paul's line to rejoice in the Lord always.
On the wreath, its candle is often rose, not purple. Even the quiet house has a day when the joy breaks in early.

how: Catholic families keep Advent at home with a wreath of four candles lit week by week, sometimes a Jesse tree, Advent hymns and quieter evenings; when to put up the Christmas tree differs from home to home.

games.why: the Church calls Advent devout and joyful expectation. an early tree can be joy that waits, not joy that skips ahead.

practice: Make a small Advent plan in three steps. First the wish: one thing you'd want your December evenings to hold, a candle at dinner, ten quiet minutes, a carol saved for Christmas.
Then the obstacle that will get in its way, the schedule, the phone, being tired, and the plan: when that happens, what you'll do instead. Hold that one sentence for the rest of the sit.
